prose:
The readable opening of a New York Times profile follows John Urschel from professional football to mathematics and describes targeted use of AI in papers. It quotes a mentor favoring assistance on specific obstacles over producing an opaque proof, while Urschel raises questions about younger researchers' futures.

This is a partial profile, not a full evaluation of the papers or a causal study of academic employment. Reported mathematical achievements and usage statements were not independently proof-checked. A personal career transition and mentor assessment do not establish universal replacement of mathematicians or guaranteed career advice. No research, contact or career action was taken.
highlights: Source opening includes biographical reporting and interviews
AI assistance is described as targeted collaboration
Underlying mathematical proofs were not checked
Mentor praise is an attributed assessment
Early-career concerns are questions, not measured job effects
